# Review 001: R0006 (design mode)
Inputs: main 660ccae plus the uncommitted prep: `tracker/rafts/R0006/{R0006-raft-browser.md,check.sh}`, `tracker/issues/c0042/{c0042-raft-browser.md,check.sh,acceptance/*.spec.luau}`; existing `scripts/tracker/{main,store}.luau`, `scripts/tracker.sh`, `scripts/check.sh`, `.github/workflows`. Probed in a scratch worktree (since removed) using the author's prototype and the marked 18.0.14 tarball (the sha256, 46,891 bytes, no `</script`, no `<script` after its single `<!--`, and ASCII-only all confirmed).

### F1 [high] Nothing automated runs the page script: a page with no working JavaScript passes every Checked criterion
Where: c0042 "Acceptance criteria" (AC2), "Unknowns" Residual; R0006 "Risks" (second bullet)
Evidence: I replaced `scripts/tracker/board.html` in the scratch copy with a stub that has the six element ids, `{{MARKED}}`, `{{DATA}}` and one script whose whole body is `thisIsNot valid javascript (((`. `bash tracker/issues/c0042/check.sh` then gave PASS on AC1–AC4 (AC5 only failed because the skill line was missing). AC2 only greps for `id="tab-active"` and the other ids, so a page that shows nothing passes it. The user's request is about navigating in a browser: arrow keys, the pane, tabs, search, highlighting. All of that lives in untested JS, and only OC1 covers it. The tracker skill says Observed criteria "do not block the merge", so a blank page can be merged. The design's mitigation, "the prototype's scripts pass `node --check`", is about the prototype, not about what the executor will ship. Some decisions still sit in JS even though the raft claims "everything a test can check is decided in Luau": the case-insensitive id normalisation (`r0040`→`R0004`, `F0100`→`f0011`), the choice of first tab ("Active if non-empty, else Waiting"), and whether a jump target is a list row or pane-only. c0042's Solution also promises "a search index" that the `Model` type doesn't contain.
Fix: (a) Move the remaining decisions into the model and spec them in `model.spec`: `search: {[lowercased id]: home id}` and `initialTab`. (b) Add a Checked AC6 that pulls the non-JSON inline scripts out of the generated page and runs `node --check` on each. Ideally it also smoke-runs the page script against a small DOM stub: the list renders `#tabs[initialTab]` rows, and a search for `c0041` selects R0005 in the Done tab. Node is on the dev hosts and on GitHub's ubuntu-latest runners; if you won't rely on it, say so in SETUP.md. At minimum, add a Judged JC1 with a rubric ("the code reviewer generates the page, runs every inline script through `node --check`, and loads it in a browser or DOM stub; any script error fails"), so a broken page can't be merged without a ruling.

### F2 [medium] On `main` the Active tab is always empty, and in-progress rafts show as "ready" in Waiting
Where: c0042 Problem ("what's active"), Design "Status" and "Tabs"; OC1 step 1
Evidence: `tracker.sh start` makes its `active/` move commit on the raft branch. The squash merge then takes the raft from backlog straight to `done/` on main (see `git log --stat -- tracker/rafts`: every raft goes `{ => done}`). The root checkout sits on `main`, and so will the user when they run `tracker.sh board --open`. There, a raft being executed in a worktree shows as backlog with `design: ready`, so it lands in Waiting, and Active is empty. Probing the prototype on the real tracker gives `active` = `{}`. OC1 already hedges this ("or Waiting, if nothing is active"). The user asked to see "what's active", and the design never tells them this view can't show it from `main`.
Fix: Get a user decision and record it in the Problem's decisions. One option is to also mark a backlog raft `active` when a local or remote branch `R####-*` exists for it. That's deterministic for a given repo state, but it has to be specced, and it makes the output depend on git refs, so RC1's "same data" becomes "same files + refs". The other is to state in Non-goals that Active reflects only the checkout the board is generated in.

### F3 [medium] Unfinished dependencies on unrafted issues are ignored, so a blocked raft is shown as top level
Where: c0042 Design, "Membership and dependencies" ("issues without a raft add nothing") and "Top level"
Evidence: The user's binding definition is that top level means "no *unfinished* dependencies". Take a raft whose member issue has `depends_on: [f0016]`, where f0016 is in the backlog with no raft. The raft gets `dependsOn = {}` and `topLevel = true`, so it's listed in Waiting as ready to go, although it's blocked. This isn't hypothetical: 34 of the real tracker's issues are raftless (the whole f0016–f0033 plan), with chains of `depends_on` between them. Rafting any of them before their dependencies triggers it. No spec case covers a dependency on a raftless issue.
Fix: Specify that a member issue's `depends_on` naming an existing raftless issue that isn't `done` makes the raft not top level. Expose those issues in a new field, `blockedBy: { string }` (sorted), shown in the pane under Depends on. Add a fixture issue and a `model.spec` case for it.

### F4 [medium] The top-level filter on the Active and Done tabs can hide rafts, and a dependency cycle hides rafts from every list
Where: c0042 Design "Tabs" and "Top level"; Usability ("every item is reachable")
Evidence: `tabs[t]` lists only top-level rafts, whatever the tab. An active raft that depends on a raft still in the backlog (for example, one started on a branch cut before its dependency merged) is `topLevel = false`, so it vanishes from Active. It appears only as a Dependents link inside a Waiting raft's pane. A done raft whose dependency isn't done vanishes from Done the same way. If two waiting rafts depend on each other through issue `depends_on` (a plausible authoring slip), neither is top level and neither is anyone's reachable dependent from a list, so both are findable only by typing their id. None of these cases is specified or specced.
Fix: Apply the top-level filter to Waiting only; Active and Done list every raft in that state, which is what "filter by done/active/waiting" suggests. If you keep the filter everywhere, specify the cycle and cross-tab cases. Either way, add a fixture case to `model.spec`.

### F5 [medium] Model edge cases are unspecified, and AC3 wouldn't notice an issue with no home
Where: c0042 Design `board.luau` types, "Membership", "`home`"; `acceptance/cli.spec.luau` third case
Evidence:
- An issue whose `raft:` names a raft that doesn't exist (after a renumber, or an unpushed placeholder raft) isn't a member, per "that raft must exist". The design never says whether it is "raftless". An implementation that treats it as neither has no `home` entry for it and shows it nowhere.
- `cli.spec` compares only raft directories with `m.rafts`. It never checks that every issue directory on disk has a `home` key, so that implementation passes.
- The No raft entries' `topLevel` and `single` values aren't specified (the prototype uses `true`).
- `Issue.type` doesn't say whether it comes from frontmatter or from the id prefix (`store.typeOf` uses the prefix).
- The body of a document with no frontmatter isn't specified.
Fix: Specify each of these: a dangling `raft:` counts as raftless and is homed to `none:<tab>`; pseudo entries have `topLevel = true` and `single = false`; `type` comes from frontmatter, falling back to the prefix; with no frontmatter the body is the whole file. Extend the cli spec's real-tracker case so that every `^[fdc]%d%d%d%d$` directory under `tracker/issues{,/active,/done}` is a key of `m.home`, and add a dangling-`raft:` fixture issue to `model.spec`.

### F6 [low] The page's character encoding is never specified or checked
Where: c0042 Design, "The page", Layout
Evidence: The tracker documents are full of non-ASCII (`—`, `→`, `≠`, `│`, `▼`, `“ ”`), and the list uses `—` for No raft. The design's layout lists the header, tabs, search, list and pane, but not `<meta charset="utf-8">`. The prototype happens to include it; an executor working from the document may not. A browser that doesn't guess UTF-8 on a local file then shows mojibake, and nothing in `page.spec` catches it.
Fix: Add `<meta charset="utf-8">` to the Layout bullet and assert it in `page.spec` (for example, it appears before the first `<script`).

### F7 [low] Smaller page and CLI behaviours an executor would have to guess
Where: c0042 Design, "The page" and "`tracker.sh board`"
Evidence:
- **Page**: nothing says which row is selected after →/← (first row, or the one remembered per tab), what the list and pane show for an empty tab (Active, normally; see F2), or what ↓/↑ do while the pane shows a pane-only dependent raft. Nor does it say that ids and titles are HTML-escaped before going into list and pane markup: a title containing `<` or `&` breaks the markup.
- **CLI**: `scripts/tracker.sh` does `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."`, so a relative `--out` resolves against the repo root, not the caller's cwd, and this is undocumented. Whether a failing `open` or `xdg-open` fails the command is unspecified.
- **Vendored file**: `marked.umd.js` ends in `//# sourceMappingURL=marked.umd.js.map`, which makes devtools request a missing file (harmless, but it contradicts "nothing loads").
Fix: One line each in the Design: the first row is selected on a tab switch; an empty tab shows "Nothing here" and an empty pane; ↓ from a pane-only view selects the first row; titles and ids are escaped; `--out` is relative to the repo root; an `open` failure warns but exits 0. The source map line can stay, because it's pinned by sha, but note it.

Verdict: changes
